lineup:C:4426354:w5.title: Wilson over Pickens, the sequel nobody asked for
lineup:C:4426354:w5.text: Week 5 again: Michael Wilson started at receiver while George Pickens went off from the bench. At this point Pickens should just mail in his own start/sit advice.

pos:K1:FLEX7.title: Kicker is pulling more weight than the flex spot
pos:K1:FLEX7.text: Your kicker ranks first in the league while flex, the wild-card spot, lags near the bottom. Nobody drafts a kicker to carry the offense, yet here we are.

proj:under:4567104:4360761.title: Your kicker is outperforming your receiver
proj:under:4567104:4360761.text: Fix the receiver spot before you fix your faith in projections. Will Reichard keeps beating his; Michael Wilson keeps missing his. ESPN's model trusts Wilson more than your own eyes should.

lineup:B:4259545:w1.title: Mostly the right calls, a few bench regrets
lineup:B:4259545:w1.text: Biggest miss: Week 1, starting Emeka Egbuka (11.3) at flex, the wild-card spot, while D'Andre Swift put up 32.4 on your bench, where points don't count.

pos:WR1:TE8.title: Receivers are carrying this roster solo
pos:WR1:TE8.text: Your receivers lead the league while your tight ends anchor the bottom. Spend the next add on a tight end before your receivers file for workers' comp.

proj:over:4430878:4360248.title: Smith-Njigba is making the projections look conservative
proj:over:4430878:4360248.text: Jaxon Smith-Njigba treats his projection like a floor, not a ceiling. Kyle Pitts Sr. can't say the same about his.

lineup:C:4241416:w1.title: Chuba Hubbard made the bench the better lineup
lineup:C:4241416:w1.text: Trust the bench over the flex call next time it's this close. Week 1 is the only real bruise on an otherwise clean season: Jaylen Waddle got the flex nod while Chuba Hubbard went off from the bench instead.

pos:FLEX2:QB8.title: The quarterback curse, now with a league rank to prove it
pos:FLEX2:QB8.text: Flex, the wild-card spot, ranks near the top for you. Quarterback ranks dead last, which at this point is less a stat and more a diagnosis.

proj:under:4429615:4572680.title: Zay Flowers is quietly having a great season
proj:under:4429615:4572680.text: Zay Flowers blew past his projection again. Tucker Kraft is still waiting to clear his.

lineup:C:4248528:w1.title: The season's oldest bench miss
lineup:C:4248528:w1.text: Quinshon Judkins got the flex nod over Christian Watson in Week 1, and Watson went off from the bench. It's the only miss from that week still on the books.

pos:TE1:RB7.title: Tight end carries this roster, running back drags it
pos:TE1:RB7.text: Your tight ends rank first in the league, your running backs near the bottom. The next waiver claim has one obvious lane to run in.

proj:under:4248528:3929630.title: Christian Watson keeps making the bench call look worse
proj:under:4248528:3929630.text: The flex spot keeps betting on the wrong back. Christian Watson has outplayed his projection for weeks; Saquon Barkley keeps coming up empty against his.

lineup:C:4685278:w7.title: The bench outplayed the starting lineup
lineup:C:4685278:w7.text: Week 7's regret: Jalen Coker got the start at receiver while Luther Burden III had himself a day from the bench. The bench earned a seat at the big-kid table that week.

pos:RB3:K8.title: The kicker is the only thing holding this back
pos:RB3:K8.text: Running back is a strength, kicker is dead last. It's the cheapest fix on the roster, and the waiver wire is practically begging to help.

lineup:B:4431459:w5.title: Your one bench regret, and it's a small one
lineup:B:4431459:w5.text: Keep the bench this honest and the dings stay rare. Week 5's only real miss: Harold Fannin Jr. got the tight end nod while Tyler Warren outproduced him from the bench, the lone smudge on an otherwise clean record.

pos:RB1:WR8.title: Running back is doing the heavy lifting
pos:RB1:WR8.text: Your running backs rank at the top of the league while your receivers sit at the bottom. The next wire move should be a receiver, not another running back you don't need.

proj:over:4430737:4870795.title: Kyren Williams keeps beating the spreadsheet
proj:over:4430737:4870795.text: Kyren Williams has spent the whole season outrunning his own projection. Makai Lemon hasn't been able to say the same about his. ESPN's model might want to double check its math.

lineup:C:4431299:w4.title: Rashee Rice gave you nothing, literally
lineup:C:4431299:w4.text: Don't make the same read twice. Week 4: Rashee Rice started at receiver and gave you a complete blank, while Rome Odunze produced from the bench instead.

pos:QB1:FLEX8.title: Quarterback is the strength, flex is the sinkhole
pos:QB1:FLEX8.text: Your quarterback ranks first in the league while flex, the wild-card spot, ranks dead last. Whatever's starting there now should not still be starting there.

proj:under:3918298:4429160.title: Josh Allen is outrunning his own projection
proj:under:3918298:4429160.text: Josh Allen has basically stopped checking his own projection, he's so far past it. De'Von Achane wishes he could say the same about his.

lineup:C:3916148:w7.title: Tony Pollard had the game Henry was supposed to have
lineup:C:3916148:w7.text: Week 7: Derrick Henry got the start at running back while Tony Pollard erupted from the bench instead. Not every bench decision needs forgiveness, just this one.

pos:WR2:RB8.title: Receivers are fine, running back is the fire
pos:WR2:RB8.text: Your receivers rank near the top of the league while running back sits dead last. That's not a tweak, that's the whole waiver budget.

proj:under:4431452:4870808.title: Drake Maye is outplaying the rookie hype around him
proj:under:4431452:4870808.text: Drake Maye keeps making his own projection look conservative. Jeremiyah Love hasn't managed the same against his. The arm is covering for the legs here.
